description: Unified Admin UI + IAM + JWT + Basic Auth + API Keys for multi-tenant Dynamic CRUD API platforms. v2.1.1 adds a "Register as API" button to the Tenant console's Access page, for v2.1.0's registered-API retry endpoint (POST /access/loginlink/apis/register) — previously reachable only directly, with no console UI for it. v2.1.0 makes CrudApi a registered API (resource server) in LoginLink, per ADR 2026-10-17-crudapi-as-loginlink-api: previously the data API only ever trusted one specific app's own client ID as its audience per workspace, so a second app (e.g. a separate dashboard product) signing its own users in through its own LoginLink app could never call the data API — its tokens were always addressed to itself, never to CrudApi. Now CrudAdmin registers CrudApi as its own API inside each workspace's LoginLink organisation (new Host Setting loginlink.api_identifier, configurable, re-registers everywhere already connected when changed), and the data API's bearer-token check accepts a token addressed to that identifier, resolving the workspace by organisation instead of by audience — safe because a workspace can now only ever connect to its own LoginLink organisation, never the platform's top-level one and never one another workspace already uses (new refusals on both connect paths). An optional per-workspace allowed-apps list restricts which apps may call this way. Separately: the data API's bearer-token check used to read an "email" claim straight off the access token, but LoginLink never puts email there by design (ID-token/userinfo only) — fixed by fetching it from LoginLink's /userinfo instead (cached, best-effort), now flowing through to the audit log's actor display. v2.0.1 adds "Unregister" to a database's Actions menu on the tenant console's Databases page — removes it from the workspace's own registry (CORS origins, row policies, rate limits and cached config state go with it) without ever touching the underlying database itself, which this platform didn't create and has no way to drop. Closes the only remaining gap in letting a tenant actually reach "holds nothing" to delete itself: API keys (Keys page) and sessions (End session) already had a self-service path, databases didn't. v2.0.0 is a platform-scale rewrite of the admin console: a unified Access model (roles, permissions, grants inspector, access catalog/report) replaces the separate Roles/Policies/Users/ProvisioningKeys/IssuanceKeys/JwtSessions/TenantSessions/ApiClients pages; a two-tier Developer API key system (platform-scoped and workspace-scoped keys, with routed capability grants) replaces ad hoc key handling; LoginLink adds tenant self-service login links (token validator, role pusher, per-tenant people/data access, a dedicated tenant-slug login page) as an alternative to password/JWT login; Managed Database provisioning adds policy-gated, script-driven database creation and admin script execution with fingerprinting; Storage & data replaces the old Backup and Migrate-to-MySQL pages with a single page covering the data folder inventory, SQLite file registry, recovery kit, and a MySQL migration wizard, plus a live, no-restart switch onto a freshly-provisioned or hand-entered MySQL store for the Setup wizard's own storage step; a new Dashboard overview and a Surfaces page (what every page/key/credential can reach) round out the console. Breaking: /admin/backup, /admin/basicauth, /admin/cors, /admin/databases, /admin/issuancekeys, /admin/jwtsessions, /admin/migratemysql, /admin/policies, /admin/provisioningkeys, /admin/roles, /admin/tenantsessions and /admin/users are removed; their data and capabilities now live under Access model, Storage & data, and Developer API. Earlier versions (back to 1.6.0) added a signed per-database cross-app handoff, tenant self-service database registration, and the initial IAM/JWT/Basic Auth/API Key admin console — see the project changelog for details.
